rendered: The micropores are smaller than the electrolyte's solvent molecule: they are too small to accommodate the solvent molecule (∼0.7 nm in diameter)[1]. The sodium ion is far smaller, the metal ion (only ∼0.2 nm in diameter) must[2] so it cannot enter the pores with its solvent shell. It is forced to desolvate at the surface of the microporous host and transport[3] independently to the sulfur[4], forming a quasi solid-state reaction at the cathode rather than a conversion reaction with ions moving through the electrolyte.
